gen-mystery-quest-gf-huninn: Mystery Quest looks bookish and nostalgic, with open jaws on its curves; Huninn is a sans-serif whose strokes never swell. Old-fashioned charm up top, a modern, businesslike hand below.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-inter-tight: Nostalgic, bookish Mystery Quest curls its open-jawed curves above compact ascenders. Inter Tight keeps its sans lines flat and unmodulated, with short ascenders, so paragraphs run along smoothly.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-karla: Mystery Quest is bookish and nostalgic, all open jaws and compact ascenders. It is made for atmosphere, while Karla, a sans with a stocky, tall middle band, is made for steady text.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-kedebideri: Bookish Mystery Quest tucks compact ascenders above its curves, every one with an open jaw. Kedebideri, a sans with a skyward x-height plus rounded, inviting letters, makes paragraphs feel approachable.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-khula: Khula, a sans-serif with a tall midsection like a squat brush-pen belly, holds its curves open. And Mystery Quest, bookish and nostalgic, gives the display flourish up top.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-krub: Storybook swagger up top: Mystery Quest has open jaws and compact ascenders. But Krub, with pen-lifted curves and a pronounced x-height, keeps long paragraphs moving with a contemporary feel.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-kufam: Neon-sign tubing for a body, a storybook feel for the heading. Mystery Quest brings nostalgic open jaws, while Kufam, a sans-serif, draws tubular letters whose bodies dominate the line.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-lexend: Big, friendly lowercase meets old-book charm: Lexend, a sans-serif, keeps its curve thickness constant. And Mystery Quest supplies the bookish, nostalgic voice, with open jaws on each curve.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-lexend-deca: Lexend Deca draws a plain, unshaded sans line that never swells, with terminals stopping short and capitals dwarfed by big lowercase. Mystery Quest adds bookish, nostalgic character up top.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-liter: Mystery Quest wears its bookish, nostalgic side in open-jawed curves and compact ascenders. Liter, a sans with no stroke contrast, gives round forms wide mouths and lowercase great vertical presence.
